messages.subject: Rhipe v0.64
parts:
From the git commit


commit 8b305a47d2243d40024069a74adc088dd621ed29
Author: Saptarshi Guha <saptars...@gmal.com>
Date: Thu Oct 21 22:30:02 2010 -0700

- Version is 0.64
- Most, not all, of the functions that talk to Hadoop use a java
server which is started with library(Rhipe)
This is auto restarted in case of errors
- Users can access sequence/map files in a streaming fashion
ushing 'rhstreamsequence', the documentation discusses this.
- This function in conjunction with 'rhbiglm.stream.hdfs' can be
used with 'biglm' for out-of-core regression (though not in parallel)
- Discussion of using biglm is incomplete


If i start writing a blog,i'll include an example of doing linear regression
using RHIPE. E.g. I did VoIP regression, ~850MM rows,12GB across 72 cores.

jitter ~ constant+traffic.rate*remote.site (interaction assumed)

where remote.site is a factor with 27 levels and traffic.rate is a continuous
variable. To compute the beta estimates, two steps are required

1) compute levels of remote.site
2) compute X'X and X'Y

Computation (2) was grossly inefficient (no optimizations just used the
model.matrix function and multiplied things, much less data can be sent over the
network if a little though it applied)

Also note, this is susceptible to size of the values, so one needs to
scale and also there are
possibly round off errors.

Despite this, the regression took *10 minutes 40 seconds*

I didn't compute SSE etc, but this would be much faster.

I checked the same computation (for a smaller data sets 550MB,30.8 MM rows) with
biglm package and got the same results which is reassuring.

Cheers
Saptarshi
